payload.name: Resume-evidence pair for activity questions
payload.description: When a question asks what activity someone resumed, took up again, or returned to after a long time, search for past hobby/interest evidence and pair it with a recent activity event before answering.
content: If a question asks what activity someone resumed, took up again, or returned to after a long time/gap, search for preference and profile memories about past hobbies/interests (e.g., '<person> used to love <activity>', '<person> hobby') as well as event memories, before answering.

Use a resumption answer only when evidence includes both a past absence/gap statement for the activity and a later event/state of the same activity; a single same-period event is not sufficient to show a resumed activity.
If the first retrieval surfaces only unrelated same-period events, re-search with candidate activity terms and re-check preference/state memories before selecting an answer.

solves: An agent can mistake an unrelated event in the target period for the resumed activity. For questions using resume, take up again, return to, after a long time, or after a gap, require both a past absence/gap statement and a later event/state of the same activity. Does not apply to ordinary dated-activity questions without a resumption cue.
